column1: # winprofile.ini escape vectors. See doc/winprofile-ini.md for the codecs and
# httrack-works/winprofile-table/DESIGN.md for why this is data rather than a
# callable function: no front end can call another's codec from its unit tests.
# raw uses \r \n \t \\ for those four bytes and is otherwise literal ASCII. The
# file is ASCII only: winprofile.ini declares no charset, the three front ends
# do not agree on one, and a non-ASCII vector passes in one place and mangles in
# another with nothing here to show the difference.
# state=agreed: all three encode raw to encoded and decode it back. Assert both
# state=divergent: they do not agree, encoded is empty, and the note says how.
# A consumer SKIPS these and COUNTS the skip; a silent pass would make the
# marker a way to hide cases from the test meant to catch them.
